statement: Let N = 3^4 5^3 7^2 11 13 ... 61 = 277093800961598968947975375 and c0 = 67 N = 18565284664427130919514350125 (Washington-Yang, arXiv:2008.04787). Call an odd n >= 3 a violator if sigma(n) >= (e^gamma/2) n loglog n. Then N is a violator and no odd n with N < n < c0 is a violator (and none up to 1e60; none with N < n among the 884 odd violators found up to 1e120).

independent_enumeration.definition: candidates = odd n in [N+1, c0-1] with sigma(n)/n >= f(N+1) where f(L) = (e^gamma/2) loglog L = 3.65922201459838; every violator n >= L has sigma(n)/n >= f(L) because f is increasing

scans.robin_sanity_k0: code/03-odd-robin-threshold/coprime_k0.out.txt (the 26 known Robin exceptions for n >= 3, largest 5040)

caveats: Completeness of the candidate enumeration rests on a provable pruning inequality (Lagrangian bound in method A, an elementary bound in method B) and on two independent implementations agreeing; it is not formalised in Lean.
The equivalence RH <=> odd inequality for n >= c0 is Washington-Yang Theorem 1.2 ; the sharp form RH <=> odd inequality for n > N follows from it and the gap result.

decisive_margins.method: exact rational sigma(n)/n; mpmath at 120 digits and python-flint balls at 400 bits agree in every printed digit
